digest.component_or_area: reconciler inbound-probe dispatch chain and deletion semantics
propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer because differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes expects jira_key in local_state but run_differs passes a fetched Jira snapshot whose entries never carry jira_key

Confirmed hard-delete of a still-locally-present ticket resurrects immediately via same-pass (inbound, delete) -> (inbound, probe) path (c244), contradicting prior-art deletion semantics that reject resurrection (Unito, Kubernetes IgnoreNotFound)

Deletion-vs-aged-out discrimination is already implemented twice and verified live on DC (outbound_differ._safe_get_issue, binding_walk.py:187-196), making the inbound-probe arm architecturally redundant

The inevitable eventual resurrection path (3 confirmed-404 note_absent calls retire binding, unbound local ticket gets outbound create) must be guarded by is_retired_local check to enforce operator ruling that deleted Jira issues must not be resurrected
drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions suppression must remain because the caller passes legacy (prev, curr) pair; removing it alongside any migration would un-suppress unsound legacy arms
The dead chain and resurrection implementation are removed; tombstone guard + unretire API make deletion permanent-by-default yet reversible, restoring operator intent without same-pass re-create
